title: Establish uniform deformation rings before shaping a smooth profile
preconditions: the target surface is intended to deform as one continuous smooth form
the local topology can support a traversable quad ring
the current ticket identifies the affected region and supplies a valid loop-cut target/parameters
required_observations: ring spacing along the deformation axis
base-cage quad aspect ratios in the affected region
profile or silhouette deviation before and after shaping
evaluated surface for buckling, pinching, and manifoldness
action_policy: Establish the full primary extent first, then distribute enough rings uniformly before applying proportional, lattice, or similar broad deformation.
Use only enough rings to represent the curvature and output scale; the transfer used 13 axial rings and 12 radial vertices, not a blanket high-density mesh.

After the uniform base is established, move rings to match the target profile where the reference demands non-uniform curvature; uniform setup is a controllable starting distribution, not a ban on purposeful local density.
Do not apply this hint when the surface is intentionally stepped, the ring path is interrupted by poles/triangles, or a ticket has not localized a valid loop-cut target.
expected_effects: lower profile approximation error for the same ring count when the alternative contains accumulated manual-step spacing/radius error
more even side-quad aspect ratios before deformation
a smoother and more controllable evaluated highlight flow
failure_predicates: the new ring does not traverse the intended quad region
added density creates pinching or unnecessary complexity without measurable silhouette improvement
another relevant view or surface channel regresses
recovery: reject or rollback the scoped loop-cut decision
use a local reroute, lattice, curve/profile construction, or fewer purposefully placed rings when uniform rings are not suitable

planner_hint.reason: The transferred experiment showed that uniform pre-distribution materially improved profile accuracy and quad density at the same topology budget.
planner_hint.expected_effect: Create a controllable, evenly distributed ring scaffold before the scoped smooth deformation.
verification: confirm the loop traversed the intended quad ring only
measure ring spacing and affected-region quad aspect ratios
reapply or preview the deformation and compare the profile/silhouette
inspect the evaluated surface and all relevant views for regression

sources.description: Blender Guru deliberately demonstrates uneven manual extrude-and-scale spacing, then establishes the full height and adds uniformly spaced loop cuts before proportional deformation.

The source lesson was independently spot-checked in the in-app browser and replayed through the committed Gemini video-understanding pipeline; the transfer claim remains grounded in the older tighter timestamp study rather than the generated source metadata.

experiments.limitations: The negative control deliberately encodes uneven spacing and small deterministic manual radius errors. The result validates the tutorial's demonstrated failure mode on one radial product form; it does not prove that every manually stepped mesh is inferior or that all deformations require uniform density.

version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS transfer; source tutorial used Blender 2.78.5 UI
status_note: A predeclared different-shape transfer passed both the modeling lab and an independent fresh-process verifier. The skill is planner-actionable only for matching localized tickets with scene-owned operation parameters; no real held-out asset runtime use has occurred yet.
